::: {.result}
**Question.** Which part of the sound sets each of the four aspects?

**Answer.** Write the sound as a sum of fading pure tones. Pitch comes from their frequencies, loudness from their overall size, timbre from their relative sizes and spacing, and duration from how fast they fade.
:::

## The sound as a sum of pure tones {#sum}

The sound at your ear is the air pressure there, measured from the average air pressure: a function $p(t)$ of the time $t$ in seconds. Page 1 let you hear the four aspects; this page looks inside $p(t)$ for what sets each one.

The simplest sound is a **pure tone**, $p(t) = \sin(2\pi f t)$, the sound of a tuning fork. It repeats $f$ times a second; $f$ is its **frequency**, in hertz (Hz).

A note played on an instrument and left to ring is, to a good approximation, a sum of pure tones that fade:[^sum]
$$
p(t) = \sum_{n} c_n\, e^{-t/\tau_n} \sin(2\pi f_n t + \varphi_n).
$$
Term $n$ is a **partial**, numbered from the lowest frequency up. It has four numbers:

- $f_n$, its frequency;
- $c_n$, its starting size;
- $\tau_n$, its fading time: the factor $e^{-t/\tau_n}$ shrinks it by $e \approx 2.7$ every $\tau_n$ seconds;
- $\varphi_n$, its phase: where in its cycle it starts.

A bowed or blown note is the same sum without the fading, for as long as the player keeps going. Why an instrument's sound has this form, and where its numbers come from, is pages 3 to 5. This page asks only which numbers you hear as what.

## Reading the four aspects off p(t) {#read}

### Pitch: the common base of the $f_n$ {#pitch}

When every partial's frequency $f_n$ is a whole-number multiple of one frequency in the range we hear as pitch (about 30 Hz to 5 kHz),[^range] or very nearly, the pitch of the note is the largest such frequency $f$.[^pitch] The reason: if every $f_n$ is a multiple of $f$, then after $1/f$ seconds every term has completed whole cycles, so the steady sum starts again. The sound repeats $f$ times a second, and the ear hears that rate as the pitch. In the mixer's close-up, the wave starts again at every gray line.

Two consequences you can hear in the mixer:

- **No partial needs to sit at $f$.** Preset *No 1st partial*: $c_1 = 0$, so the lowest partial is at $2f$, yet the sound still repeats $f$ times a second and the pitch stays.[^mf]
- **Only the partials that are there count.** Preset *Even only*: the partials at $2f, 4f, 6f, 8f$ are all multiples of $2f$, so the pitch jumps up an octave.

When the $f_n$ are not whole-number multiples of one such frequency (move the stretch), the sum never repeats at a rate we hear as pitch, and the pitch blurs.

::: {.derive}
<details><summary><span class="label">Proof</span>A sum of sines repeats exactly when every frequency is a multiple of one frequency <span class="needs">averages of products of sines, and divisibility</span></summary>

*Claim.* Let $p(t) = \sum_{n=1}^{N} c_n\sin(2\pi f_n t + \varphi_n)$ with distinct frequencies $f_n > 0$ and sizes $c_n \ne 0$. A time $P > 0$ is a period of $p$, meaning $p(t+P) = p(t)$ for every $t$, exactly when every $f_nP$ is a whole number. Hence $p$ is periodic exactly when every ratio $f_n/f_1$ is a fraction, and its shortest period is then $1/g$, where $g$ is the largest frequency of which every $f_n$ is a whole-number multiple.

*Proof.* If every $f_nP$ is a whole number, each term completes whole cycles in time $P$, so $p(t+P) = p(t)$. Conversely, suppose $p(t+P) = p(t)$ for every $t$. The identity $\sin(\theta+\delta) - \sin\theta = 2\sin(\delta/2)\cos(\theta + \delta/2)$ gives, with $s_n = \sin(\pi f_n P)$ and $\theta_n = \varphi_n + \pi f_nP$,
$$
0 = p(t+P) - p(t) = \sum_{n=1}^{N} 2c_n s_n \cos(2\pi f_n t + \theta_n).
$$
Write $\langle w\rangle = \lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T} w(t)\,dt$ for the long-run average. For $\gamma \ne 0$ the integral of $\cos(2\pi\gamma t + \delta)$ over $[-T, T]$ stays bounded, so its average is $0$. By $2\cos A\cos B = \cos(A-B) + \cos(A+B)$, for $a, b > 0$ the average $\langle\cos(2\pi a t + \alpha)\cos(2\pi b t + \beta)\rangle$ is $\tfrac12\cos(\alpha - \beta)$ if $a = b$ and $0$ if $a \ne b$. Multiply the displayed sum by $\cos(2\pi f_k t + \theta_k)$ and average: every term with $n \ne k$ vanishes, leaving $c_k s_k = 0$. Since $c_k \ne 0$, $\sin(\pi f_kP) = 0$, so $f_kP$ is a whole number.

For the shortest period: if $p$ has a period $P$, each $f_n/f_1 = (f_nP)/(f_1P)$ is a fraction. Conversely, if every $f_n/f_1$ is a fraction, a common denominator gives $f_n = q_nh$ with whole numbers $q_n$ and $h = f_1/D$. Let $d$ be the greatest common divisor of the $q_n$ and $g = dh$, so $f_n = m_ng$ with whole numbers $m_n$ whose greatest common divisor is $1$. By the first part, $P$ is a period exactly when every $m_n gP$ is a whole number. That holds if $gP$ is a whole number; conversely, Bézout's identity gives whole numbers $u_n$ with $\sum u_nm_n = 1$, so $gP = \sum u_n(m_ngP)$ is a whole number. So the periods are the whole-number multiples of $1/g$. If every $f_n$ is a multiple of some $g'$, then $1/g'$ is a period, hence a multiple of $1/g$, so $g' \le g$. $\square$

*Fading sounds* cannot repeat exactly: $p(t) = p(t + rP)$ for every whole number $r$, and the right side tends to $0$ as $r$ grows, so $p$ would be $0$. They nearly repeat: when every $f_n$ is a multiple of $g$ and every term fades with the same time $\tau$, each cycle is the one before shrunk by the factor $e^{-1/(g\tau)}$.

</details>
:::

### Loudness: the overall size of the $c_n$ {#loudness}

Multiplying every $c_n$ by the same factor $k$ multiplies $p(t)$ by $k$ and changes nothing else: the same $f_n$, the same ratios, the same $\tau_n$. For steady partials the sound's power, the long-run average of $p(t)^2$, is $\tfrac12\sum_n c_n^2$ (the cross terms average to $0$, by the averages in the proof above), so it grows by $k^2$, and the level by $20\log_{10}k$ decibels. In the pictures, the wave and every stem grow by the same factor. Ten decibels more sounds roughly twice as loud.[^stevens] Moving one $c_n$ alone changes the overall size and the ratios at once, so it changes both loudness and timbre.

### Timbre: the ratios of the $c_n$, the spacing of the $f_n$, and how they start {#timbre}

With pitch, loudness and duration fixed, three things in $p(t)$ are left, and they make the timbre:[^timbre]

1. **The ratios $c_n/c_1$.** Presets *Pure*, *Mellow*, *Bright* and *Hollow*, page 1's four timbres, have the same pitch and the same power and differ only in these ratios: compare their stems. Strong high partials sound bright; only odd partials sound hollow, like a clarinet.
2. **How close the $f_n$ sit to whole-number multiples.** Move the stretch: smooth, then shimmering, then a clang (preset *Bell-like*).
3. **How the sizes change in time, especially at the start.** In the formula every term starts at full size at $t = 0$, a sudden start like a pluck, and fades at its own rate. Tick *high partials fade faster*: the note starts bright and turns mellow, as a plucked string does. The start is a strong cue: without it, listeners name instruments much less well.[^attack]

The phases $\varphi_n$ matter much less: changing them changes the shape of the wave, but the timbre far less than changing the sizes does.[^phase] Sounds outside the formula add to the timbre too: the scrape of a bow, a breath, a hammer's thump, and the gradual start of a bowed or blown note.

### Duration: the $\tau_n$ {#duration}

Term $n$ shrinks by a factor of 1000 in about $7\tau_n$ seconds, since $e^{-6.9} \approx 1/1000$; in the mixer, the whole note shortens or lengthens with $\tau$. So a ringing note lasts a few times its longest fading time, unless the player damps it: a key released, a hand on a drumhead. A bowed or blown note does not fade while the player keeps going; it lasts as long as they play.

::: {.result}
**Takeaway.** A note is a sum of fading pure tones,
$$
p(t) = \sum_n c_n\, e^{-t/\tau_n}\sin(2\pi f_n t + \varphi_n),
$$
and each aspect is read off different numbers in it: **pitch** off the frequencies $f_n$ (their common base), **loudness** off the overall size of the $c_n$, **timbre** off the ratios of the $c_n$, the spacing of the $f_n$ and how the sizes change over time, and **duration** off the fading times $\tau_n$.
:::

## Back to the two questions {#questions}

Page 1's two questions are now questions about these numbers:

1. **Why does a piano have a pitch and a drum not?** Why are a piano's $f_n$ whole-number multiples of one frequency, or very nearly, and a drum's not?
2. **Why do instruments sound so different?** Why do their ratios $c_n/c_1$, the spacing of their $f_n$, and their fading times $\tau_n$ differ?

Both need to know where $p(t)$ comes from: how an instrument's motion becomes the pressure at your ear. That is [page 3](../from-instrument-to-ear/index.qmd).

[^sum]: N. H. Fletcher and T. D. Rossing, [*The Physics of Musical Instruments*](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-0-387-21603-4), 2nd ed., Springer, 1998, chapters 1 and 2 (free vibrations with damping; the modes of strings and bars). Pages 3 to 5 derive this form.
[^pitch]: B. C. J. Moore, [*An Introduction to the Psychology of Hearing*](https://auditory.org/postings/2012/87.html), 6th ed., Emerald, 2012, chapter 6, on the pitch of complex tones. The rule is for a single note: in a chord the ear sorts the partials into several notes, and some sounds, such as bells, are heard at a pitch set by only some of their partials.
[^range]: Melodic pitch is heard from about 30 Hz (D. Pressnitzer, R. D. Patterson and K. Krumbholz, [The lower limit of melodic pitch](https://www.pdn.cam.ac.uk/node/469), *J. Acoust. Soc. Am.* 109 (2001), 2074–2084) up to about 4 or 5 kHz for pure tones (A. J. Oxenham and colleagues, [Pitch perception beyond the traditional existence region of pitch](https://experts.umn.edu/en/publications/pitch-perception-beyond-the-traditional-existence-region-of-pitch/), *PNAS* 108 (2011), 7629–7634). Without this range the rule would give tones at 100 and 159 Hz, whose largest common base is 1 Hz, a pitch of 1 Hz.
[^mf]: This is the *missing fundamental*; it keeps a deep voice's pitch over a telephone line, which carries little below about 300 Hz. Wikipedia, [Missing fundamental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missing_fundamental).
[^stevens]: S. S. Stevens, ["On the psychophysical law"](https://doi.org/10.1037/h0046162), *Psychological Review* 64 (1957), 153–181; Wikipedia, [Sone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sone). How loud a given power sounds also depends on the frequencies, as page 1 noted.
[^timbre]: Wikipedia, [Timbre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timbre); Moore, [*An Introduction to the Psychology of Hearing*](https://auditory.org/postings/2012/87.html), 6th ed., 2012, chapter 8.
[^attack]: E. Saldanha and J. F. Corso, ["Timbre cues and the identification of musical instruments"](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.1919317), *J. Acoust. Soc. Am.* 36 (1964), 2021–2026, as summarized in K. Siedenburg, [Specifying the perceptual relevance of onset transients for musical instrument identification](https://www.uni-oldenburg.de/f/6/dept/mediphysik/ag/musik-wahrnehmung/siedenburg2019transients.pdf), *J. Acoust. Soc. Am.* 145 (2019), 1078–1087.
[^phase]: R. Plomp and H. J. M. Steeneken, ["Effect of phase on the timbre of complex tones"](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.1911705), *J. Acoust. Soc. Am.* 46 (1969), 409–421, as summarized by J. W. Beauchamp, [AUDITORY list](https://auditory.org/postings/2010/868.html), 2010.

<script src="core.js"></script>
<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";
  var C = Core, SR = 44100;
  // Sample peaks are kept at or below 0.55: core.js sends sound through a gain of 0.55 and a compressor with threshold -10 dB,
  // and 0.55 * 0.55 = 0.30 is below it.
  var PEAK = 0.55, A = 0.3;   // A: sample value of a partial of size c = 1

  // ---- a sound as an array of samples ----
  function synth(parts, dur, attack, release) {
    var N = Math.floor(dur * SR), d = new Float32Array(N);
    parts.forEach(function (p) {
      if (p.f > SR / 2.3 || p.f <= 0 || !p.amp) return;
      var w = 2 * Math.PI * p.f / SR, c = Math.cos(w), s = Math.sin(w), re = 1, im = 0, e = p.amp;
      var dec = isFinite(p.tau) ? Math.exp(-1 / (p.tau * SR)) : 1, n1 = isFinite(p.tau) ? Math.min(N, Math.ceil(p.tau * SR * 9)) : N;
      for (var n = 0; n < n1; n++) { d[n] += e * im; var nr = re * c - im * s; im = re * s + im * c; re = nr; e *= dec; }
    });
    var a = Math.max(1, Math.floor(attack * SR)), r = Math.max(1, Math.floor(release * SR));
    for (var n = 0; n < a && n < N; n++) d[n] *= 0.5 - 0.5 * Math.cos(Math.PI * n / a);
    for (var m = 0; m < r && m < N; m++) d[N - 1 - m] *= 0.5 - 0.5 * Math.cos(Math.PI * m / r);
    return d;
  }
  var cur = null;
  function stop(tc) { if (!cur) return; var t = C.ac().currentTime; cur.g.gain.setTargetAtTime(0, t, tc || 0.006); cur.src.stop(t + 10 * (tc || 0.006) + 0.02); cur = null; }
  function play(d) {
    var a = C.ac(); stop();
    var b = a.createBuffer(1, d.length, SR); b.getChannelData(0).set(d);
    var src = a.createBufferSource(), g = a.createGain(); src.buffer = b; src.connect(g); g.connect(C.out); src.start();
    cur = { src: src, g: g };
  }

  // ---- drawing (as on page 1) ----
  function axes(x, W, H, d) { x.clearRect(0, 0, W, H); x.strokeStyle = C.rgb("--grid"); x.lineWidth = d; x.beginPath(); x.moveTo(0, H / 2); x.lineTo(W, H / 2); x.stroke(); }
  function label(x, s, px, py, d) { x.fillStyle = C.rgb("--muted"); x.font = (10 * d) + "px 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace"; x.textAlign = "center"; x.fillText(s, px, py); }
  function drawWhole(cv, data, T, scale, m0, m1) {
    var d = C.fit(cv), W = cv.width, H = cv.height, x = cv.getContext("2d"), half = H / 2 - 4 * d;
    axes(x, W, H, d);
    x.fillStyle = C.rgb("--accent", 0.16); var a0 = m0 / T * W, a1 = Math.max(a0 + 3 * d, m1 / T * W); x.fillRect(a0, 0, a1 - a0, H);
    x.strokeStyle = C.rgb("--accent"); x.lineWidth = Math.max(1, d); x.beginPath();
    for (var i = 0; i < W; i++) {
      var j0 = Math.floor(i / W * T * SR), j1 = Math.floor((i + 1) / W * T * SR), lo = 0, hi = 0;
      for (var j = j0; j < j1 && j < data.length; j++) { var v = data[j]; if (v < lo) lo = v; if (v > hi) hi = v; }
      if (hi - lo > 0) { x.moveTo(i + 0.5, H / 2 - hi * scale * half); x.lineTo(i + 0.5, H / 2 - lo * scale * half); }
    }
    x.stroke();
    for (var s = 1; s < T; s++) label(x, s + " s", s / T * W, H - 3 * d, d);
  }
  function drawZoom(cv, data, t0, w, scale, period) {
    var d = C.fit(cv), W = cv.width, H = cv.height, x = cv.getContext("2d"), half = H / 2 - 6 * d;
    axes(x, W, H, d);
    x.strokeStyle = C.rgb("--grid"); x.lineWidth = d;
    for (var k = Math.ceil(t0 / period); k * period <= t0 + w; k++) { var px = (k * period - t0) / w * W; x.beginPath(); x.moveTo(px, 0); x.lineTo(px, H); x.stroke(); }
    x.strokeStyle = C.rgb("--accent"); x.lineWidth = 2 * d; x.beginPath();
    for (var i = 0; i <= W; i++) {
      var tt = (t0 + i / W * w) * SR, j = Math.floor(tt), f = tt - j, v = j + 1 < data.length ? data[j] * (1 - f) + data[j + 1] * f : 0, py = H / 2 - v * scale * half;
      if (i) x.lineTo(i, py); else x.moveTo(i, py);
    }
    x.stroke();
  }

  // ---- the mixer's state ----
  var NP = 8, cs = [], eC = [];
  var eF = document.getElementById("mxF"), eLev = document.getElementById("mxLev"), eB = document.getElementById("mxB"), eT = document.getElementById("mxT"), eHi = document.getElementById("mxHi");
  var box = document.getElementById("mxC");
  for (var q = 1; q <= NP; q++) {
    var row = document.createElement("div"); row.className = "slider";
    row.innerHTML = '<label for="mxc' + q + '" style="min-width:1.6rem"><i>c</i><sub>' + q + '</sub></label><input type="range" id="mxc' + q + '" min="0" max="1" step="0.01" style="flex:1 1 5rem"><output id="mxc' + q + 'o"></output>';
    box.appendChild(row);
  }
  function fBase() { return Math.round(110 * Math.pow(4, parseFloat(eF.value) / 1000)); }            // 110 to 440 Hz
  function Bv() { var s = parseFloat(eB.value) / 1000; return 0.1 * s * s * s; }                    // 0 to 0.1
  function tauV() { var v = parseFloat(eT.value); return v >= 100 ? Infinity : 0.1 * Math.pow(40, v / 99); }   // 0.1 to 4 s, then steady
  function gain() { return Math.pow(10, parseFloat(eLev.value) / 20); }
  function partials() {
    var f = fBase(), B = Bv(), tau = tauV(), g = gain(), out = [];
    for (var n = 1; n <= NP; n++) {
      var r = n * Math.sqrt(1 + B * n * n) / Math.sqrt(1 + B);
      out.push({ n: n, ratio: r, f: f * r, c: g * cs[n - 1], tau: isFinite(tau) && eHi.checked ? tau / n : tau });
    }
    return out;
  }
  // presets: sizes scaled to the same power (sum of c^2 / 2 = 1/2, a pure tone of size 1)
  function norm(a) { var s = 0; a.forEach(function (v) { s += v * v; }); var k = 1 / Math.sqrt(s); return a.map(function (v) { return Math.round(100 * v * k) / 100; }); }
  var PRE = {
    pure: { c: [1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] },
    mellow: { c: [1, 1 / 4, 1 / 9, 1 / 16, 1 / 25, 1 / 36, 1 / 49, 1 / 64] },
    bright: { c: [1, 1 / 2, 1 / 3, 1 / 4, 1 / 5, 1 / 6, 1 / 7, 1 / 8] },
    hollow: { c: [1, 0, 1 / 3, 0, 1 / 5, 0, 1 / 7, 0] },
    nofirst: { c: [0, 1 / 2, 1 / 3, 1 / 4, 1 / 5, 1 / 6, 1 / 7, 1 / 8] },
    even: { c: [0, 1 / 2, 0, 1 / 4, 0, 1 / 6, 0, 1 / 8] },
    bell: { c: [1, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.45, 0.4, 0.35], B: 0.1 }
  };
  var PRETXT = {
    pure: "Pure, one partial only",
    mellow: "Mellow, sizes 1, 1/4, 1/9, …, 1/64: weak high partials",
    bright: "Bright, sizes 1, 1/2, 1/3, …, 1/8: strong high partials",
    hollow: "Hollow, only the odd partials",
    nofirst: "No 1st partial, <i>c</i><sub>1</sub> = 0: the lowest partial is at 2<i>f</i>, but every <i>f<sub>n</sub></i> is still a multiple of <i>f</i>, so the <b>pitch stays</b>",
    even: "Even only, with only <i>f</i><sub>2</sub>, <i>f</i><sub>4</sub>, <i>f</i><sub>6</sub>, <i>f</i><sub>8</sub>: all multiples of 2<i>f</i>, so the <b>pitch jumps an octave</b>",
    bell: "Bell-like: many strong partials, stretched far off the gray lines"
  };

  // ---- what changed: highlight the symbols and the table columns, and say what you hear ----
  var lastSym = [], lastCol = [], lastStem = -1;
  function said(html, syms, cols, stem) {
    document.getElementById("mxWhat").innerHTML = html;
    lastSym = syms; lastCol = cols || syms; lastStem = stem == null ? -1 : stem;
    document.querySelectorAll("#mxFormula [data-sym]").forEach(function (s) { s.classList.toggle("hl", lastSym.indexOf(s.getAttribute("data-sym")) >= 0); });
  }

  // ---- drawing everything ----
  var data = null, WT = 3, Z0 = 0.05, ZW = 0.02;
  function build() {
    var P = partials(), tau = tauV(), dur;
    if (isFinite(tau)) { var tm = 0; P.forEach(function (p) { if (p.c) tm = Math.max(tm, p.tau); }); dur = Math.min(4, Math.max(0.4, 7 * tm)); }
    else dur = 1.5;
    data = synth(P.map(function (p) { return { f: p.f, amp: A * p.c, tau: p.tau }; }), dur, 0.003, isFinite(tau) ? 0.03 : 0.04);
    var pk = 0; for (var i = 0; i < data.length; i++) pk = Math.max(pk, Math.abs(data[i]));
    if (pk > PEAK) for (var j = 0; j < data.length; j++) data[j] *= PEAK / pk;     // only for extreme settings: avoid distortion
    return P;
  }
  function gcd(a, b) { while (b) { var t = b; b = a % b; a = t; } return a; }
  function draw() {
    var P = build(), f = fBase(), B = Bv(), tau = tauV(), lev = parseFloat(eLev.value);
    document.getElementById("mxFo").textContent = f + " Hz";
    document.getElementById("mxLevo").textContent = (lev < 0 ? "−" + (-lev) : "0") + " dB";
    document.getElementById("mxBo").textContent = "B = " + (B === 0 ? "0" : B < 0.01 ? B.toFixed(4) : B.toFixed(3));
    document.getElementById("mxTo").textContent = isFinite(tau) ? tau.toFixed(tau < 1 ? 2 : 1) + " s" : "steady";
    eC.forEach(function (el, i) { el.value = cs[i]; document.getElementById("mxc" + (i + 1) + "o").textContent = (gain() * cs[i]).toFixed(2); });
    var sc = 1 / PEAK;
    drawWhole(document.getElementById("mxWhole"), data, WT, sc, Z0, Z0 + ZW);
    drawZoom(document.getElementById("mxZoom"), data, Z0, ZW, sc, 1 / f);
    // repetition
    var on = P.filter(function (p) { return p.c > 0; }), msg;
    if (!on.length) msg = "silence";
    else if (B === 0) {
      var g = 0; on.forEach(function (p) { g = gcd(g, p.n); });
      var fr = f * g;
      msg = "every <i>f<sub>n</sub></i> here is a multiple of <b>" + fr + " Hz</b>: the sound " + (isFinite(tau) ? "nearly repeats (it fades)" : "repeats") + " " + fr + " times a second" + (cs[g - 1] === 0 ? ", with no partial at " + fr + " Hz" : "");
    } else msg = "the <i>f<sub>n</sub></i> are " + on.slice(0, 3).map(function (p) { return p.ratio.toFixed(2); }).join(", ") + (on.length > 3 ? ", …" : "") + " times <i>f</i>: not multiples of one frequency, so no exact repeat";
    document.getElementById("mxRep").innerHTML = msg;
    // stems at f_n / f, height c_n (absolute: a size of 1 fills the box)
    stems(P);
    table(P, tau);
  }
  var NS = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg";
  function el(tag, at, par) { var e = document.createElementNS(NS, tag); for (var k in at) e.setAttribute(k, at[k]); par.appendChild(e); return e; }
  function stems(P) {
    var svg = document.getElementById("mxStems"); while (svg.firstChild) svg.removeChild(svg.firstChild);
    var W = 320, H = 120, L = 8, R = W - 10, base = H - 16, top = 8, rmax = 8;
    P.forEach(function (p) { if (p.c > 0) rmax = Math.max(rmax, Math.ceil(p.ratio - 1e-9)); });
    function xo(r) { return L + (R - L) * r / (rmax + 0.5); }
    for (var k = 1; k <= rmax; k++) {
      el("line", { x1: xo(k), x2: xo(k), y1: top, y2: base, stroke: C.rgb("--grid"), "stroke-width": 1 }, svg);
      if (rmax <= 10 || k % 2 === 0) { var t = el("text", { x: xo(k), y: H - 3, "text-anchor": "middle", "font-size": 9 }, svg); t.textContent = (k === 1 ? "" : k) + "f"; }
    }
    el("line", { x1: L, x2: R, y1: base, y2: base, stroke: C.rgb("--muted"), "stroke-width": 1 }, svg);
    P.forEach(function (p, i) {
      if (!(p.c > 0)) return;
      var h = Math.max(1.5, (base - top) * Math.min(1, p.c)), hl = lastSym.indexOf("c") >= 0 && (lastStem < 0 || lastStem === i) || lastSym.indexOf("f") >= 0;
      el("line", { x1: xo(p.ratio), x2: xo(p.ratio), y1: base, y2: base - h, stroke: C.rgb("--accent"), "stroke-width": hl ? 4.5 : 3, "stroke-linecap": "round" }, svg);
    });
  }
  function table(P, tau) {
    var t = document.getElementById("mxTab"), cols = lastCol;
    function th(sym, html) { return '<th' + (cols.indexOf(sym) >= 0 ? ' class="hl"' : '') + '>' + html + '</th>'; }
    var h = "<tr>" + th("n", "<i>n</i>") + th("f", "<i>f<sub>n</sub></i> (Hz)") + th("c", "<i>c<sub>n</sub></i>") + th("tau", "<i>τ<sub>n</sub></i> (s)") + "</tr>";
    P.forEach(function (p, i) {
      function td(sym, v) { var on = cols.indexOf(sym) >= 0 && (sym !== "c" || lastStem < 0 || lastStem === i); return "<td" + (on ? ' class="hl"' : "") + ">" + v + "</td>"; }
      h += '<tr' + (p.c > 0 ? "" : ' class="off"') + "><td>" + p.n + "</td>" + td("f", p.f.toFixed(p.f < 1000 ? 1 : 0)) + td("c", p.c.toFixed(2)) + td("tau", isFinite(p.tau) ? p.tau.toFixed(p.tau < 1 ? 2 : 1) : "∞") + "</tr>";
    });
    t.innerHTML = h;
  }

  // ---- controls ----
  function go() { draw(); play(data); }
  for (var q2 = 0; q2 < NP; q2++) (function (i) {
    var e = document.getElementById("mxc" + (i + 1)); eC.push(e);
    e.addEventListener("input", function () {
      cs[i] = parseFloat(e.value);
      said("You changed <i>c</i><sub>" + (i + 1) + "</sub> alone: the <b>ratios</b> of the <i>c<sub>n</sub></i> change, and their overall size a little. You hear mostly <b>timbre</b> change.", ["c"], ["c"], i);
      draw();
    });
    e.addEventListener("change", function () { play(data); });
  })(q2);
  eF.addEventListener("input", function () { said("You changed <i>f</i>: every <i>f<sub>n</sub></i> = <i>n f</i> moves by the same factor. You hear <b>pitch</b> change.", ["f"]); draw(); });
  eLev.addEventListener("input", function () { said("You changed the level: every <i>c<sub>n</sub></i> is multiplied by the same factor, so the ratios stay. You hear <b>loudness</b> change.", ["c"]); draw(); });
  eB.addEventListener("input", function () { said("You changed the stretch: the higher <i>f<sub>n</sub></i> move off the whole-number multiples of <i>f</i>. You hear <b>timbre</b> change (smooth, shimmer, clang), and the pitch blur.", ["f"]); draw(); });
  eT.addEventListener("input", function () { said("You changed <i>τ</i>: every fading time <i>τ<sub>n</sub></i>. You hear <b>duration</b> change.", ["tau"]); draw(); });
  [eF, eLev, eB, eT].forEach(function (e) { e.addEventListener("change", function () { play(data); }); });
  eHi.addEventListener("change", function () { said(eHi.checked ? "Now <i>τ<sub>n</sub></i> = <i>τ</i>/<i>n</i>: the high partials fade first. You hear the <b>timbre</b> change over time, bright at the start and mellow later." : "Now every partial fades with the same time <i>τ</i>.", ["tau"]); go(); });
  document.querySelectorAll("[data-mx]").forEach(function (b) {
    b.addEventListener("click", function () {
      var k = b.getAttribute("data-mx"), p = PRE[k];
      cs = norm(p.c); eB.value = Math.round(1000 * Math.cbrt((p.B || 0) / 0.1));
      said("Preset: " + PRETXT[k] + (k === "nofirst" || k === "even" ? "." : ", with the same power. You hear <b>timbre</b> change."), k === "bell" ? ["c", "f"] : ["c"]);
      go();
    });
  });
  document.getElementById("mxPlay").addEventListener("click", go);
  document.getElementById("mxStop").addEventListener("click", function () { stop(0.03); });

  cs = norm(PRE.bright.c);
  window.addEventListener("resize", draw);
  C.onTheme(draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>
